intro: Before you is the Theatre at Hierapolis, from the 2nd century AD. Cut into the slope above the travertines of Pamukkale, it was built for 15,000 people. Its stage front, three ranks of columns deep, survives in large part and was re-erected between 2004 and 2014.
spot-1: Now you are looking at the orchestra, a half circle about twenty metres across in the model. Keep in mind that this is a derived figure, not a measured one.
spot-2: Now you are looking at the stage front. Three ranks of columns deep, it was re-erected between 2004 and 2014.
spot-3: Now you are looking at the diazoma, the walkway that divides the twenty rows below from the twenty-five above.
spot-4: Now you are looking at the cavea. Eight stairways cut it into seven wedges, and it held 15,000 spectators.
uncertainty: Finally, what this model does not know. The same source describes the theatre in two ways: as having 50 rows, and as having 20 below and 25 above. The model follows the second and raises 45. The diameters of the cavea and the orchestra are not measured; they are derived from the row count and a 0.75 m tread. The statuary of the stage front and the imperial box are not modelled.
